errors.english: This is not the case; if it were to possess parts
errors.why: de lta ma yin te here means 'otherwise' (supporting the claim that it must be partless), not a denial of the preceding statement.

note: Faithful rendering of Vinītadeva's argument on atoms and conventional existence; only a misleading connective.

errors.english: By seeing that non-existent things like a rabbit's horns do not exist, this argument actually establishes
errors.why: The reason ('being uncreated') is seen to occur in non-existents such as a hare's horn, so it proves the subject space non-existent; nothing about seeing that horns do not exist.

fix.find: By seeing that non-existent things like a rabbit's horns do not exist, this argument actually establishes
fix.replace: Since this reason (being uncreated) is seen in non-existent things such as a rabbit's horns, it actually establishes

errors.english: An connection with the actual nature of the subject
errors.why: In this list of viruddha reasons (cf. the preceding chos kyi rang gi ngo bo dang 'gal ba) the category is contradiction of the subject's own nature (dharmisvarūpaviparīta); 'brel ba is a slip for 'gal ba.

note: Generally accurate on svayam/iṣṭa in the pakṣa definition, but the hare's-horn example is misconstrued.

errors.english: the Tathagatas [note: the Buddhas], who bring supreme light, performed
errors.why: It is the one Tathāgata (the Buddha, Śuddhodana's son; Skt. tathāgatas singular) who honoured his father's body and built a stūpa, which is why the monks then question him.

fix.find: the Tathagatas [note: the Buddhas], who bring supreme light, performed
fix.replace: the Tathagata [note: the Buddha], who brings supreme light, performed

note: Tibetan verses rendered faithfully, Sanskrit lines transliterated; one plural for the Buddha distorts the narrative.

errors.english: just like impermanence and the like
errors.why: skad cig ma nyid is momentariness (kṣaṇikatva), not impermanence (mi rtag pa).

fix.find: Therefore, just like impermanence and the like, this is
fix.replace: Therefore, just like momentariness and the like, this is

note: The fire/smoke causal argument is followed accurately; 'Indra's head' is left literal (it is the anthill example) but defensibly so.

errors.english: in order to refute that which harms the self
errors.why: bdag la gnod par byed pa is the objection that harms 'us' (the author's selflessness position), which the following verse states as the opponent's consequence; 'the self' suggests the ātman.

note: Accurate commentary on BCA 9.73-75 (past/present mind, banana tree); one ambiguous referent at the transition.

errors.english: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
errors.why: The sūtra says the niśraya teacher in turn does these services for the pupil, except asking (his) permission; the roles are reversed and dri ba/zhu ba is asking permission (āpṛcchā), not questioning.

fix.find: **The dependent also performs these duties for the teacher, with the exception of questioning.**
fix.replace: **He [the teacher] too should do these for him [the pupil], except asking permission.**

errors.english: This means that while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher in tasks such as managing
errors.why: It is the teacher (gnas) who, apart from not asking permission, must help the pupil with bowl and robe work as listed above.

fix.find: This means that while the one in dependence should not interrogate the teacher, they must assist and support the teacher in tasks such as managing
fix.replace: This means that the teacher, except that he need not ask permission, must assist and support the pupil in tasks such as managing

errors.english: must not live without relying on a preceptor (Upādhyāya) or a resident teacher (Ācārya).
errors.why: One under ten years must not act as preceptor, nor as niśraya teacher, nor live without dependence: these are the 'three' asked about next.

fix.find: must not live without relying on a preceptor (Upādhyāya) or a resident teacher (Ācārya).
fix.replace: must not act as a preceptor (Upādhyāya) or as a teacher of dependence (Ācārya), nor live without dependence.

errors.english: **Not if they lack even one of the qualities mentioned in the sets of five.**
errors.why: The sūtra disqualifies one who possesses none of the pentads described below (any one pentad suffices), not one who lacks a single quality.

fix.find: **Not if they lack even one of the qualities mentioned in the sets of five.**
fix.replace: **Not one who possesses none of the sets of five described below.**

errors.why: lnga phrugs are pentads (sets of five qualifications); what follows is the content of a pentad, not 'five qualities', and the English then lists only four.

errors.english: the state of being under a tutor's instruction
errors.why: The commentary glosses this as freeing the preceptor quickly from the saṅgha's penalty (gnod pa), not separation from the state of dependence.

note: Vinaya duties of teacher and dependent are systematically misassigned and the ten-year rule and pentad clause are misread.

errors.english: That is not the nature of reality itself. By whom [note: is this perceived]?
errors.why: The root verse (PV 3 'tad atattvavidaḥ sarve') says these are not knowers of reality; the commentary then asks who is meant.

fix.find: That is not the nature of reality itself. By whom [note: is this perceived]?
fix.replace: Therefore they are not knowers of reality. Who are they?

errors.english: much like a person who is the object of desire
errors.why: mngon par 'dod pa here means 'accepted/asserted': the person you posit (the perceiver of the previous side), not an object of desire.

errors.english: In this way, the cause of their attachment is shown.
errors.why: The honorific mnga' ba refers to the Buddha: this explains why the Buddha appears to have attachment (by teaching as things are seen), not the cause of beings' attachment.

errors.english: Just as an elephant looks back
errors.why: The image (gajanimīlana) is the elephant feigning not to see, closing its eyes; 'looks back' is not in the text.

note: The PV 3 passage on Buddha's 'elephant gaze' is broadly followed but the root verse and several referents are misread.

errors.english: Indeed, a noble birth prevents one from falling into utter insignificance.
errors.why: The verse says that in some, a great fault (frivolity) negates even the highest birth, which the following lines (well-born men like dogs) illustrate; the English says the opposite.

note: Narrative and gem verses well rendered; one verse line about noble birth is inverted.
Accurate rendering of the asiddha section with correct technical vocabulary (pakṣadharmatā, Digambara example, definition of death).

errors.english: then it would be reasonable to call it an assembly meeting in a single object
errors.why: 'du ba here is the Vaiśeṣika relation of inherence (samavāya), 'inherence in a single object' (ekārthasamavāya), not an assembly; the forest-number example turns on inherence.

note: Argument against the variegated whole and successive grasping is followed well; the inherence terminology is blurred at the opening.
